# Best portable power stations for a CPAP

Any pure sine wave unit can run a CPAP. The real choice is how many nights you get per charge, especially with the heated humidifier on, which roughly doubles power draw.

## My picks

**Best value: Bluetti AC180 (1,152 Wh), $499**
- Runs about 3.1 nights humidifier off and 1.4 nights humidifier on, per [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).
- It has a 12 V car port, so you can use your CPAP maker's DC cord for extra runtime. Its warranty is 5 years.
- The code AFF5OFF takes it to $474.05 at Bluetti's store, per [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180).
- It weighs about 35 lb, which is heavy for travel.
- **Buy:** [Bluetti AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you.

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (1,024 Wh), about $700**
- [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/) picks it as the quietest option (about 20 dB under 200 W). It has a 10 ms UPS switchover and recharges in about 49 minutes.
- It runs about 2.7 nights humidifier off and 1.7 nights on, using Tested Watts' figures.
- It isn't expandable.
- I don't have a direct purchase link for it. Prices and "Check on Amazon" links are on [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).

**Best if you want whole-home backup too: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (1,024 Wh, expandable to 5 kWh), about $719**
- It switches over in under 10 ms and stays under 30 dB up to 600 W. See [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/).
- It weighs 27.6 lb.

**Cheapest for two dry nights: EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro, $389**
- BuyerSheet lists about 2 nights humidifier off and 0.9 nights on. See [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).
- It's a better pick than the RIVER 3 Plus if you want more than one night.

## Things to know
- **Humidifier:** Estimates vary by site. Tested Watts assumes about 520 Wh per night with it on, and PowerStationBench assumes about 720 Wh. If you use it, buy toward the larger end. Your CPAP's wattage label or a watt meter will give the real number.
- **Small units:** The RIVER 3 Plus (286 Wh) is described by one site as covering a full night. Others, including [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/) and BuyerSheet, put it at under one night even with the humidifier off. I'd skip it unless you'll only use it for short trips.
- **Jackery:** Jackery says its power stations aren't recommended for medical devices. Check that note and ask your CPAP maker before choosing the Explorer 1000 v2.
- **Switchover:** Look for a UPS that switches in about 10 ms or less, so therapy keeps running if the grid fails while you sleep.
- **Prices:** They vary a lot between sources. For example, PowerStationBench lists the AC180 at $449 on Amazon, so check current prices before buying.

This is general information, not medical advice. If you depend on your CPAP, talk to your provider about a backup plan.

**Sources:** [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180), [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/), [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap)

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the humidifier, and how many nights of backup you want, I can narrow this to one pick.
